s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic pruritic skin condition with erythematous papules and lymphoid infiltrate
salient_findings: Erythematous papules with crusts and excoriations on the trunk and upper extremities
Scales and fissures on the lower lip with sparing of the surrounding skin
key_facts: Topical corticosteroids did not control symptoms
Physical examination revealed erythematous papules, crusts, and excoriations
Scales and fissures on the lower lip
Normal blood test results including antinuclear antibodies and complement
Skin biopsy showed spongiosis, erosions, and nodular lymphocyte infiltrate
Phototest with solar simulator showed delayed erythema to UV-A

shortlist.label: Lymphomatoid papulosis
shortlist.why_kept: Nodular lymphocyte infiltrate and erythematous papules

shortlist.label: Pityriasis lichenoides chronica
shortlist.why_kept: Erythematous papules and scales on the lower lip

shortlist.label: Jessner's lymphocytic infiltrate
shortlist.why_kept: Lymphoid infiltrate in the dermis and erythematous papules

shortlist.label: Cutaneous lymphoid hyperplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Nodular lymphocyte infiltrate and germinal centers in the dermis

raw.rationale: The presence of erythematous papules, crusts, and excoriations, along with the skin biopsy showing spongiosis, erosions, and a nodular lymphocyte infiltrate with CD20 positive and BCL-2 negative cells, supports this diagnosis. The lack of response to topical corticosteroids and the specific findings on biopsy also point towards a lymphoma rather than a benign dermatitis.

rejected.label: atopic dermatitis
rejected.why: The lack of response to topical corticosteroids and the specific biopsy findings are not typical for atopic dermatitis

rejected.label: bullous pemphigoid
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and biopsy findings do not match those of bullous pemphigoid, which typically presents with blisters

rejected.label: Mycosis Fungoides
rejected.why: While mycosis fungoides is a type of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, the specific biopsy findings and clinical presentation in this case are more suggestive of a cutaneous T-cell lymphoma without specifying mycosis fungoides

rejected.label: Sézary Syndrome
rejected.why: Sézary syndrome is a more aggressive form of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma with systemic involvement, which is not indicated in this case
